limitation: Color presence does not validate bone count, anatomical registration, left/right identity, bone lengths or 3D pose. See visual review.

visualReview.method: 18 full-body frames and 18 enlarged upper-body crops at 3 Hz; color and background-marker detection on all 180 frames. Not an exact 3D reconstruction audit.
visualReview.identity: Single gray Fukuchan game-style actor; recognizable face and original clothing geometry remain.
visualReview.camera: Three fixed markers tracked through all 180 frames, maximum displacement 0.355 px.
visualReview.coloredOverlay: Three color families remain present in all frames, but this is not left/right or topology preservation.
visualReview.leftRight: FAIL: initial magenta arm becomes cyan; both arms appear cyan by 0.33 s and in subsequent sampled poses.
visualReview.topology: FAIL: extra cyan finger/hand line segments and a yellow loop around the pelvis appear, despite explicit no-finger and no-extra-node instructions.
visualReview.registration: The overlay follows the broad body movement, but it is a generated reinterpretation, not the supplied exact game-rig projection after the first frame.
visualReview.arms: Upper arms spread away from the torso in several swing poses. The result does not establish a natural relaxed arm reference.
visualReview.gaze: Generally upright and forward in sampled poses.
visualReview.timing: Walking and final standing visible. The actor becomes more frontal than the initial oblique side pose.
visualReview.decision: Keep as an exploratory Wan capability sample. Reject as accurate skeleton ground truth or direct replacement for the game walking clip.
visualReview.interpretation: In this single first-frame-plus-text trial, visual skeleton styling persisted but explicit rig topology and left/right colors did not. This does not establish the limits of every Wan conditioning approach.
